name: commit-graph
title: Commit Graph
description: The model behind CommitHistory: commits, a one-pass nesting of merged branches under their merge, the rows that show with merges open or closed, git log --graph style lanes laid out lazily, and a commit message parser for file and branch chips.
docs: `createCommitGraph(commits)` reads commits newest first, children before parents (`git log --topo-order`), once: each merge's merged-in branch nests under it as the block of commits right after it that only it reaches. `updateCommitGraph(previous, commits)` reuses the previous graph when the history only grew at the end (an older page) or only changed content (a pending commit that finished), so a page costs its own rows. `visibleRows(graph, expanded)` skips closed merges' blocks; `createLaneLayout(graph, visible, { maxLanes })` gives each shown row its node's lane and the lanes running into, out of and past it, computed the first time a row (or one below it) is asked for and kept; an octopus merge's parents past `maxLanes` count as `overflow`. `parseCommitMessage` turns backticked paths into file segments, `` `branch:name` `` into branch segments and git's merge subjects ("Merge a into b") into branch chips; `commitSubject` reads a message as plain text and `createCommitFinder(graph)` finds a commit by id, hash prefix or subject. `createBranchModel(graph, branches, { base, staleAfter })` works out each branch's commits ahead of the base along its first parent, its merge-base, how far behind it is and whether it's active, stale or merged, in O(commits + commits ahead), and gives each a stable lane colour (`tag`). For the branches view, `createLaneLayout` takes `reserve` (the base's head on lane 0), `headTag` (a head's lane colour), `keepLanes` (a branch keeps its lane down to its merge-base) and `maxLanes`, past which lanes are counted in `hidden` rather than drawn; a row costs O(maxLanes + parents) however many lanes are open.
